question: Why does every finished film keep a second-by-second log of the music in it?
answer: Because royalties are paid from it. The cue sheet lists every cue, its composers and publishers, how it is used, as background, theme or song performed on screen, and its exact duration. Collecting societies read it to pay writers whenever the film is broadcast. Twelve seconds of a radio in the background earns its share.
move: Money follows the paperwork, so whoever keeps the log decides who gets paid.
ask: In my own money matters, who keeps the log that decides who gets paid?
reference: Kohn and Kohn, Kohn on Music Licensing, 4th edition, Wolters Kluwer, 2010
